title: Does TRAINED (PonderNet-style) halting buy LENGTH generalization where inference-time entropy halting failed - or is stochastic depth all you need?

config.title: Does TRAINED (PonderNet-style) halting buy LENGTH generalization where inference-time entropy halting failed - or is stochastic depth all you need?
config.hypothesis: On an n-RASP-L-style task whose required number of sequential steps grows linearly with input length (prefix-parity under a 2-token attention window: position i needs K >= i-1 loops), a weight-tied block trained with a PonderNet halting head learns to spend MORE loops on longer inputs and therefore extrapolates further in LENGTH than the same block trained at a fixed loop count - and at least matches the proven stochastic-depth recipe (k ~ U{1..K_train}).

dataset.name: synthetic prefix-parity (cumulative XOR): input BOS x_1..x_L with x_i in {0,1}, target y_i = XOR(x_1..x_i)
dataset.source: generated in run.py from the seed (torch.Generator, no external data)

arms.name: fixed_K7
arms.note: (a) the naive baseline: tied block trained at a FIXED K=7, lengths U{2..8}

arms.name: stoch_depth
arms.note: (b) the proven recipe from 2026-07-25_loop-test-time-compute: k ~ U{1..7} per batch with L = k+1 so every supervised position is exactly computable at that depth

arms.name: ponder
arms.note: (c) PonderNet: per-position halt head, expected-loss weighting over N=7 unrolled steps, KL to a geometric prior; lengths U{2..8}

arms.name: ponder_stoch
arms.note: (d) hybrid: PonderNet loss but the unroll horizon is itself stochastic, N ~ U{L-1 .. 7} - tests whether trained halting needs the stochastic-depth ingredient to extrapolate
